# Brand OS

This portal is a **template**. The name “EXAMPLE Brand”, the colors, and the type stacks are pipeline samples. They are not an approved identity.

## What lives here

The Brand OS is the umbrella. The Business OS sits inside it, in `brand/business-os`. One brand, one private repository. A mascot and gamification can be turned off without deleting the template support for them.

## Status versus approval

A field can be unanswered, unknown, skipped, not applicable, draft, in review, or approved. Coverage is not approval. The dashboard prints both.

## Interview

Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one question, stores your answer with provenance, and updates a draft. It does not promote that draft to a rule unless you approve it.

Say `unknown`, `skip`, `not relevant`, or `decide later` when you do not have a fact. The agent must not fill the gap with a plausible brand.

## Restricted data

Finance figures, revenue-share notes, and board locations are restricted. They are kept out of the public documentation build, the public search index, and the default agent tools.


## Brand Strategy

# 01 — Brand Strategy

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** brand.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Explain why the brand exists, who it serves, and how decisions are made. Audience, offer, and value proposition are referenced from the Business OS so the brand book cannot drift.

## Decision this informs

Which brand choices are allowed when a tactic is tempting but off-strategy.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Personality | yes | internal | `brand.personality.traits` |
| Purpose | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.purpose` |
| Vision | optional | internal | `brand.strategy.vision` |
| Values | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.values` |
| Differentiation | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.differentiation` |
| Brand promise | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.promise` |
| Decision rule | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.decision_rule` |
| Experience principles | yes | internal | `brand.strategy.experience` |
| Trade name | canonical reference | public | `business.identity.trade_name` |
| Primary customer | canonical reference | internal | `business.customer.primary_segment` |
| Value proposition | canonical reference | internal | `business.offer.value_proposition` |
| Geography | canonical reference | internal | `business.market.geography` |
| Jobs to be done | canonical reference | internal | `business.product.jobs` |

## Guidance

Purpose, mission, vision, and promise are different sentences. Leave any of them unknown rather than paraphrasing the value proposition three times.

Personality is a working draft until approved. Archetype labels are optional tools, not a diagnosis.

Decision rules should be specific enough that a designer can say no.

Experience principles govern product, support, and marketing together.

## Inputs

- Trade name
- Segment
- Value proposition
- Geography

## Artifacts

- Purpose draft
- Personality draft
- Decision rule

## Acceptance

- A campaign brief can point at one strategy record.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/01-brand-strategy/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/brand-strategy.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE decision rule: “Do not show a feature that product.public_status does not allow.” The example is a rule shape, not this brand’s strategy.

## Do

- Link the primary segment instead of writing a second persona.
- Record the jobs-to-be-done reference next to any journey claim.
- Date the strategy and name an owner.

## Don't

- Do not invent an origin story.
- Do not claim a competitive ranking you have not sourced.
- Do not treat a mood adjective as an approved visual rule.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Canonical value proposition is referenced, not rewritten.
- [ ] Decision rule exists or is explicitly deferred.
- [ ] Personality draft is labeled draft.

## Dependencies

- `business-company`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/brand-strategy.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when the segment, offer, or stage changes.

## Metrics

- Open strategy fields
- Approved decision rules

# 02 — Verbal Identity

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** brand.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Fix the name, voice, vocabulary, and microcopy rules. Official statements are stored in the language the owner approved. This system does not auto-translate them.

## Decision this informs

Which words are allowed, required, or forbidden.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name usage | yes | internal | `brand.verbal.name_use` |
| Public name override | yes | internal | `brand.identity.public_name_override` |
| Tagline | optional | internal | `brand.verbal.tagline` |
| Tone of voice | yes | internal | `brand.verbal.voice` |
| Forbidden language | yes | internal | `brand.verbal.forbidden` |
| Localization | yes | internal | `brand.verbal.localization` |
| Microcopy principle | yes | internal | `brand.verbal.microcopy` |
| Trade name | canonical reference | public | `business.identity.trade_name` |
| Personality | canonical reference | internal | `brand.personality.traits` |

## Guidance

Record spelling, pronunciation, and what never to abbreviate.

Taglines are optional. A missing tagline stays missing.

Tone adapts by channel only after the base voice exists.

Keep Persian, English, and Turkish UI chrome separate from approved brand sentences.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/02-verbal-identity/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/verbal-identity.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE forbidden line: “The world’s most loved app.” No evidence, so it is not a template default.

## Do

- Point product microcopy at the same voice.
- List forbidden claims (superlatives, medical or financial promises) explicitly.
- Note localization owners per language.

## Don't

- Do not publish a slogan the owner has not approved.
- Do not machine-translate a legal or brand promise.
- Do not invent a pronunciation that conflicts with the owner.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Name spelling matches the canonical trade name or an approved override.
- [ ] Forbidden language includes unapproved prices and unshipped features.
- [ ] Examples in the docs are labeled EXAMPLE.

## Dependencies

- `brand-strategy`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/verbal-identity.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review before any public campaign.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 03 — Logo System

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Specify logo variants, clear space, minimum sizes, and misuse once artwork exists. The template ships a labeled placeholder, not a logo.

## Decision this informs

Which master files are approved and how they may be placed.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variants needed | yes | internal | `brand.logo.variants` |
| Clear space | yes | internal | `brand.logo.clear_space` |
| Minimum size | optional | internal | `brand.logo.min_size` |
| Misuse rules | yes | internal | `brand.logo.misuse` |
| Master location | yes | internal | `brand.logo.masters` |
| Trademark status | canonical reference | internal | `business.legal.trademark` |
| Name usage | canonical reference | internal | `brand.verbal.name_use` |

## Guidance

List the variants you need (primary, secondary, stacked, wordmark, icon, mascot lockup) without drawing them.

Clear space and minimum size stay TBD until a master exists.

Incorrect-use examples should describe the failure (“do not recolor an unapproved master”) rather than fake a competitor comparison.

Point downloads at asset ids. If the file is missing, the gallery must say so.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/03-logo-system/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/logo-system.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

The file brand/assets/logo/example-wordmark.svg is an EXAMPLE frame so the pipeline has a real file. It is not a brand mark.

## Do

- Keep placeholder SVGs marked EXAMPLE.
- Separate source files from exports.
- Record the background rules you actually need.

## Don't

- Do not trace someone else’s mark.
- Do not mark the placeholder approved.
- Do not add a ® unless the legal module says the mark is registered.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Asset id exists for every claimed master.
- [ ] Approved status is false while files are placeholders.
- [ ] Clear space is TBD or measured.

## Dependencies

- `verbal-identity`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/logo-system.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when the name or an approved master changes.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 04 — Color System

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Define color roles, themes, and contrast requirements. Hex values live in DTCG tokens. The starter palette is EXAMPLE data for the pipeline, not an approved brand palette.

## Decision this informs

Which roles exist and what contrast bar they must meet.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Color roles | yes | internal | `brand.color.roles` |
| Themes | yes | internal | `brand.color.themes` |
| Semantic colors | yes | internal | `brand.color.semantics` |
| Contrast target | yes | internal | `brand.color.contrast` |
| Print color | optional | internal | `brand.color.print` |

## Guidance

Talk about roles (primary, surface, danger) before picking hues.

Do not let an interview answer overwrite token JSON without a review of contrast.

Light and dark themes are both first-class if you ship a product UI.

Print color (coated/uncoated, spot versus process) stays a strategy note until a printer spec exists.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/04-color-system/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/color-system.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

The repo includes an accessible EXAMPLE blue (#123A73) so the docs theme and tests have a real value. Replace it after approval.

## Do

- Keep EXAMPLE tokens marked draft.
- Pair foreground and background explicitly.
- Use the token exporter instead of copying hex into Markdown.

## Don't

- Do not approve a palette that fails the stated contrast bar.
- Do not invent a cultural color meaning.
- Do not use color as the only status signal.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Contrast target is chosen.
- [ ] Token status is draft until approval.
- [ ] Semantic colors are roles, not moods.

## Dependencies

- `brand-strategy`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/color-system.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when a theme or a semantic role changes.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 05 — Typography

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Choose families, licenses, scales, and multilingual behavior. Starter tokens name EXAMPLE families and system fallbacks. No commercial font is bundled.

## Decision this informs

Which type is allowed to ship, and under what license.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type intent | yes | internal | `brand.type.intent` |
| License status | yes | internal | `brand.type.license` |
| Scale | yes | internal | `brand.type.scale` |
| RTL and locales | yes | internal | `brand.type.rtl` |
| Fallback policy | yes | internal | `brand.type.fallback` |
| Localization | canonical reference | internal | `brand.verbal.localization` |
| Third-party content | canonical reference | internal | `business.legal.third_party` |

## Guidance

Record the license and the fallback stack before a family is called approved.

RTL, Arabic/Persian shaping, and Turkish dotted I are requirements, not afterthoughts, when those languages are official.

A scale (display, headline, body, caption) can be chosen before the final family.

Do not self-host a font file you do not have rights to.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/05-typography/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/typography.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

Tokens list “EXAMPLE Sans” falling back to system UI fonts. That stack is a placeholder.

## Do

- Keep license status next to the family name.
- Define a fallback that covers the languages you approved.
- Use tokens for size and line height.

## Don't

- Do not download a random webfont into the repo.
- Do not claim a family is free without a source.
- Do not use display type for legal text.

## Review checklist

- [ ] License is TBD or cited.
- [ ] RTL behavior is decided or not applicable.
- [ ] Scale roles exist.

## Dependencies

- `verbal-identity`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/typography.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when a language or a license changes.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 06 — Mascot Identity

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Optional character system. When disabled, these questions are skipped and the docs hide the module. No artwork is generated here.

## Decision this informs

Whether a character exists and which anatomical rules are canonical.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mascot | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.enabled` |
| Character role | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.role` |
| Character personality | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.personality` |
| Anatomy rules | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.anatomy` |
| Forbidden distortions | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.forbidden` |
| Character palette | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.palette` |
| Personality | canonical reference | internal | `brand.personality.traits` |

## Guidance

Start with the model sheet and the forbidden list before expressions.

Personality of the character must fit brand.personality.traits or explicitly extend it.

Record proportions as constraints (“hands stay simple”) not as fake measurements of art you do not have.

2D, 2.5D, and 3D alignment is a decision about future production, not a render.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/06-mascot-identity/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-identity.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE configuration in the template turns the module on so the catalog is visible. A B2B init turns it off.

## Do

- Keep the module optional.
- Write forbidden distortions before style experiments.
- Use stable ids for any later art.

## Don't

- Do not generate a character and call it approved.
- Do not copy a known mascot.
- Do not require a mascot for brands that answered no.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Enabled flag matches config.
- [ ] Anatomy rules exist or the module is off.
- [ ] No source file is marked approved without a checksum.

## Dependencies

- `brand-strategy`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-identity.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review only when the character or the enable flag changes.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 07 — Mascot Expression & Pose Library

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Map product situations to catalog ids. The 90-state catalog is a proposal list with empty art slots.

## Decision this informs

Which states are in the MVP set and how they are named.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Emotion priority | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.emotion_priority` |
| Situation map | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.situation_map` |
| Intensity scale | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.intensity` |
| Angle priority | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.angles` |
| MVP states | optional | internal | `brand.mascot.mvp` |

## Guidance

Use the ids in brand/mascot. Do not rename a state by inventing a filename.

Intensity, angle, and stage compatibility are fields on every state.

Product UI states and learning contexts can be irrelevant. Mark them not applicable instead of drawing them.

The MVP subset is a production order, not a deletion of the other states.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/07-mascot-expression-pose-library/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-expression.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

Onboarding success should look up mascot.ui.success and mascot.emotion.joyful, then stop if art is missing.

## Do

- Filter the explorer by status.
- Keep missing previews labeled missing.
- Map one product moment to one primary state id.

## Don't

- Do not generate 90 illustrations to “fill the grid”.
- Do not mark draft states approved.
- Do not use a celebration state for an error.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Catalog validates at 20/20/15/15/10/10.
- [ ] MVP list is 20–30 ids.
- [ ] Each used id exists.

## Dependencies

- `mascot-identity`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-expression.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Update when a new product situation needs a state.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 08 — Mascot Evolution

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Configure how many stages exist. The six-stage egg-to-captain sequence is an EXAMPLE configuration, not a universal rule.

## Decision this informs

How many stages exist and what continuity must survive a stage change.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stage count | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.stage_count` |
| Stage story | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.stage_story` |
| Continuity | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.continuity` |
| Unlock placeholder | yes | internal | `brand.mascot.unlocks` |
| Transition | optional | internal | `brand.mascot.transition` |

## Guidance

A brand may use one stage. That is the default for a static character.

Unlock conditions are placeholders until product defines real rules.

Stage art references list compatible state ids. Missing files stay missing.

Transitions need a reduced-motion alternative.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/08-mascot-evolution/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-evolution.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE stages: egg, hatchling, explorer, trainee, pilot, captain. Replace or delete when you choose a count.

## Do

- Label the six-stage story as EXAMPLE.
- Keep silhouette continuity explicit.
- Separate visual stage from game level.

## Don't

- Do not invent XP costs.
- Do not force six stages onto a B2B brand.
- Do not discard earlier-stage recognition cues.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Stage count is configured.
- [ ] Example stages are labeled example.
- [ ] Unlock copy says placeholder.

## Dependencies

- `mascot-identity`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/mascot-evolution.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when progression rules change.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# 09 — Illustration System

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Art direction for scenes that are not the mascot model sheet: shape, light, crop, and complexity.

## Decision this informs

What an illustration is allowed to contain.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shape language | yes | internal | `brand.illustration.shapes` |
| Light and materials | yes | internal | `brand.illustration.light` |
| Complexity | yes | internal | `brand.illustration.complexity` |
| Character integration | yes | internal | `brand.illustration.character` |
| Unacceptable variations | yes | internal | `brand.illustration.unacceptable` |

## Guidance

Describe shape language and outline weight as rules a second illustrator can follow.

Scene complexity should name a maximum cast and a crop rule.

Educational diagrams and marketing scenes can differ if you say so.

If a mascot appears, it follows the mascot module. If the mascot is off, illustrations stay character-free.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/09-illustration-system/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/illustration.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: flat shapes, no fake brand characters, no stock watermark art.

## Do

- Write unacceptable variations.
- Keep stock-art policy explicit.
- Separate spot art from hero scenes.

## Don't

- Do not paste unlicensed reference art into the repo.
- Do not use a photoreal child or a real customer as a style default.
- Do not let illustration contradict product status.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Style rules exist or are TBD.
- [ ] License path is clear.
- [ ] Mascot integration matches the enable flag.

# 10 — Iconography & Graphic Elements

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.

## Purpose

Rules for UI icons, brand marks, badges, patterns, and export names.

## Decision this informs

How a symbol is drawn, named, and exported.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Icon grid | yes | internal | `brand.icons.grid` |
| Stroke and corners | yes | internal | `brand.icons.stroke` |
| Metaphors | yes | internal | `brand.icons.metaphor` |
| Badges | optional | internal | `brand.icons.badges` |
| Naming and export | yes | internal | `brand.icons.naming` |

## Guidance

Pick a grid and a stroke model before drawing a set.

Badges and stickers are not the same component as a 24px UI icon.

If motifs come from a mascot, reference the mascot id and degrade gracefully when the mascot is off.

Animated icons need a reduced-motion still.

## Fill-in record

EXAMPLE icon: brand/assets/icons/example-mark.svg is a geometric placeholder.

## Do

- Name files from the id, not from a campaign joke.
- Keep corner radius consistent with the radius tokens.
- Document optical corrections.

## Don't

- Do not mix filled and stroked sets without a rule.
- Do not use the logo as a bullet icon.
- Do not ship trademarked emoji as brand assets.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Grid is stated or TBD.
- [ ] Naming pattern exists.
- [ ] UI icons meet contrast on both themes.

## Guidance

## Do

- Name the grid per surface.
- State hierarchy: one primary action.
- Keep aspect ratios with the template that uses them.

## Don't

- Do not center everything by default and call it a system.
- Do not place text below the contrast bar.
- Do not invent device frames as requirements.

# 12 — Product UI Design System

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Foundations, components, states, and handoff. This repo documents the system and binds examples to tokens. It is not a full production component library for your app.

## Decision this informs

Which components exist, which states they need, and what accessibility bar they inherit.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Platforms | yes | internal | `brand.ui.platforms` |
| Component priority | yes | internal | `brand.ui.components` |
| Required states | yes | internal | `brand.ui.states` |
| Onboarding pattern | yes | internal | `brand.ui.onboarding` |
| UI accessibility | yes | internal | `brand.ui.a11y` |
| Handoff | yes | internal | `brand.ui.handoff` |
| Color roles | canonical reference | internal | `brand.color.roles` |
| Microcopy principle | canonical reference | internal | `brand.verbal.microcopy` |
| Accessibility intent | canonical reference | internal | `business.product.accessibility` |
| Onboarding outcome | canonical reference | internal | `business.cx.onboarding` |

## Guidance

Foundations point at DTCG tokens: color, type, space, radius, elevation, motion.

Every interactive component needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, and error where those states exist.

Patterns (onboarding, empty, success, offline, permissions) reference content rules and, optionally, mascot state ids.

Figma component names should map to the same ids. Drift is a report, not a second source of truth.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/12-product-ui-system/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/product-ui.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

The docs include an EXAMPLE token button. It demonstrates states. It is not your app’s button.

## Do

- Show focus without relying on color alone.
- Write empty and error copy against the voice rules.
- Keep dark mode on the same components.

## Don't

- Do not claim a React kit you have not shipped.
- Do not design a control that product scope excluded.
- Do not remove focus outlines.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Token ids are used in examples.
- [ ] Keyboard behavior is described for each new component.
- [ ] Handoff names match Figma when a file exists.

## Dependencies

- `color-system`
- `typography`
- `layout`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/product-ui.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

# 13 — Motion Identity

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Timing, easing, and the rules for logo, interface, and optional character motion. Tokens hold durations. Reduced motion is mandatory.

## Decision this informs

How things move, and when they must not.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Motion principles | yes | internal | `brand.motion.principles` |
| Duration feel | yes | internal | `brand.motion.duration` |
| Reduced motion | yes | internal | `brand.motion.reduced` |
| Logo motion | optional | internal | `brand.motion.logo` |
| Deliverable formats | yes | internal | `brand.motion.formats` |

## Guidance

Principles should be short enough to review a prototype against.

Durations and easings live in motion tokens. Do not hard-code a second scale in slides.

Character rigs, if any, reference mascot motion briefs.

Deliverables (Lottie, Rive, CSS, SVG, video) are choices with performance budgets.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/13-motion-identity/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/motion.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE durations: 120, 200, 320, and 480 ms. They are draft tokens.

## Do

- Provide a reduced-motion alternative for every required motion.
- Keep celebration rare.
- Document autoplay and sound separately.

## Don't

- Do not ship looping video of missing mascot art.
- Do not use vestibular-heavy motion as a brand signature by default.
- Do not claim a Lottie file you have not exported.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Token durations exist.
- [ ] Reduced motion is specified.
- [ ] Performance budget is a number or TBD.

## Dependencies

- `brand-strategy`
- `product-ui`

## Related drafts

# 14 — Sonic Branding

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** brand.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Optional sound: logos, cues, voice, loudness, and rights. Silence is a valid brand choice. Sound-off is required either way.

## Decision this informs

Whether sound exists and which rights allow it.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sound | yes | internal | `brand.sonic.needed` |
| Sonic logo | optional | internal | `brand.sonic.logo` |
| Cues | yes | internal | `brand.sonic.cues` |
| Rights | yes | internal | `brand.sonic.rights` |
| Sound off | yes | internal | `brand.sonic.fallback` |
| Name usage | canonical reference | internal | `brand.verbal.name_use` |
| Third-party content | canonical reference | internal | `business.legal.third_party` |

## Guidance

A sonic logo is not required. Many brands should answer no.

Voiceover pronunciation follows the verbal module.

Music needs a license and a mood reference the owner supplies, not a downloaded track.

Loudness targets are TBD until a sound exists. Do not invent LUFS numbers as if they were measured.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/14-sonic-branding/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/sonic.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: sound is off. No audio files are shipped.

## Do

- Keep a mute path.
- Record rights next to any cue.
- Separate UI sounds from advertising music.

## Don't

- Do not add stock audio to the repo without a license.
- Do not autoplay sound.
- Do not claim a mascot voice that was never recorded.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Need is yes or no.
- [ ] Rights are cited or not applicable.
- [ ] Sound-off behavior exists.

## Dependencies

- `verbal-identity`

# 18 — Print, Merchandise & Environment

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** design.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Physical applications: print specs, merchandise, packaging, and environments. Most brands should leave this not applicable until a real object exists.

## Decision this informs

Whether physical production is in scope and which specs are known.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Physical scope | yes | internal | `brand.print.scope` |
| Print specification | optional | internal | `brand.print.color` |
| Bleed and safe area | optional | internal | `brand.print.bleed` |
| Merchandise rules | optional | internal | `brand.print.merch` |
| Production notes | optional | internal | `brand.print.vendor` |

## Guidance

Bleed, trim, and safe area are printer specs. Do not copy a generic 3mm and call it approved.

Merchandise licensing is a legal question as well as a visual one.

Environmental graphics need viewing distance rules.

Mascot-on-product shots require the mascot module and a production note.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/18-print-merchandise/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/print.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: print is out of scope. No bleed value is approved.

## Do

- Say not applicable.
- Keep vendor contacts out of public docs.
- Separate dielines from marketing mockups.

## Don't

- Do not order merch from the EXAMPLE wordmark.
- Do not invent Pantone codes.
- Do not store supplier bank details.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Scope is in or out.
- [ ] Color spec points at the color module.
- [ ] No physical file is marked print-ready without a check.

## Dependencies

- `logo-system`
- `color-system`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/print.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review before any print spend.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.

Which surfaces are reference implementations.

# 20 — Governance & Asset Library

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** brand.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Ownership, approvals, versioning, and the asset manifest. This is how a draft becomes a rule and how a file becomes findable.

## Decision this informs

Who may approve, deprecate, and publish.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brand approver | yes | internal | `brand.gov.approver` |
| Versioning | yes | internal | `brand.gov.versioning` |
| Deprecation | yes | internal | `brand.gov.deprecation` |
| Content license | yes | internal | `brand.gov.license` |
| AI provenance | yes | internal | `brand.gov.ai` |
| Maintenance cadence | yes | internal | `brand.gov.cadence` |
| Decision rights | canonical reference | internal | `business.ops.decisions` |
| Decision rule | canonical reference | internal | `brand.strategy.decision_rule` |

## Guidance

The lifecycle is not_started, draft, in_review, approved, deprecated.

Approved visual and verbal rules change only through a proposed diff and a named approver.

The manifest stores license, visibility, checksum, and presence. Missing stays missing.

AI suggestions remain suggestions until a human approves them. Record that provenance.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/20-governance-assets/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/governance.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

The EXAMPLE wordmark is draft, public, and checksummed. The canonical mascot turnaround is absent on purpose.

## Do

- Use stable asset ids.
- Keep a change log.
- Filter public builds.

## Don't

- Do not approve a missing file.
- Do not commit secrets.
- Do not let an agent rewrite an approved rule in place.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Approver matches operations decision rights.
- [ ] Manifest validates.
- [ ] Deprecation path is written.

## Dependencies

- `business-operations`
- `brand-strategy`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/governance.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review the library on the cadence the owner sets. Default in the template is “when a rule changes”.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.

# G — Gamification

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** product.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Optional visual rules for progress, streaks, rewards, and failure. Game logic and economy live in the product, not in this visual system. Values are placeholders.

## Decision this informs

Whether game-like visuals exist and which ethics constraints they carry.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gamification | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.enabled` |
| Progress model | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.model` |
| Streak policy | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.streaks` |
| Reward ethics | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.ethics` |
| Failure tone | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.failure` |
| Character link | yes | internal | `brand.gamification.mascot_link` |
| Unlock placeholder | canonical reference | internal | `brand.mascot.unlocks` |
| Experience principles | canonical reference | internal | `brand.strategy.experience` |

## Guidance

Separate the visual state (locked, unlocked, celebrated) from the mechanic (XP, streak length).

Do not put numbers in the brand book that product has not defined.

Failure states must not humiliate. That is a brand rule, not a game-balance note.

If a mascot stage changes with progress, reference mascot unlock placeholders.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/content/gamification/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/gamification.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: streaks may exist later. No length, forgiveness rule, or reward is defined.

## Do

- Keep celebration infrequent.
- Design the muted and reduced-motion versions.
- Label every economy value as a placeholder.

## Don't

- Do not invent XP, drop rates, or streak penalties.
- Do not use loss aversion as the voice.
- Do not require gamification for a brand that turned it off.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Enable flag is explicit.
- [ ] Ethics constraint is written.
- [ ] No numeric economy is presented as real.

## Dependencies

- `product-ui`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/gamification.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review when product changes the progression model.

## Metrics

- None defined yet.



## Use case: campaign handoff

---
title: "Use case: campaign handoff"
visibility: public
sidebar_position: 6
---

## Request

Hand a campaign to design.

## Retrieval

1. Open the campaign brief template.
2. Quote `business.customer.primary_segment`, `business.offer.value_proposition`, `business.sales.pricing`, and `business.product.public_status` by id.
3. If any of those are unknown, write unknown in the brief. Do not invent a price or an availability claim.

## Result in this template

The brief can be created. It will be full of TBD until the interview records those fields.


## Use case: Instagram carousel

---
title: "Use case: Instagram carousel"
visibility: public
sidebar_position: 2
tags: 
  - use-case
---

## Request

“Create an Instagram carousel using approved brand typography.”

## Retrieval

1. Read `AGENTS.md`. Approved records outrank drafts.
2. Read `brand/content/16-social-media/overview.md`.
3. Read `brand/tokens/typography.tokens.json` and check that the status is still draft.
4. Call `get_brand_tokens` without `include_unapproved`.

## Result in this template

There is no approved typeface and no approved carousel template. Stop. Do not present the EXAMPLE font stack as the brand’s type.

## When assets are missing

Say what is missing, name the question ids `brand.type.license` and `brand.social.templates`, and wait. Do not draw stand-in brand content.


## Use case: motion clip

---
title: "Use case: motion clip"
visibility: public
sidebar_position: 5
---

## Request

Make a short motion clip.

## Retrieval

1. Read motion principles and the reduced-motion answer.
2. Use duration tokens rather than a one-off timing.
3. If the clip needs a character, use a motion brief id from `brand/mascot/motions.yaml` and stop when the fallback still is missing.

## Result in this template

Durations are EXAMPLE drafts. There is no approved logo sting and no character render. A reduced-motion still is required before any loop ships.


## Use case: onboarding mascot

---
title: "Use case: onboarding mascot"
visibility: public
sidebar_position: 3
optional_module: mascot
---

## Request

“Find the approved happy mascot pose for an onboarding success screen.”

## Retrieval

1. Check `brand.mascot.enabled`.
2. Look up `mascot.ui.success`, then `mascot.emotion.joyful` and `mascot.emotion.delighted`.
3. Read `source_assets`, `preview`, and `status`.

## Result in this template

The rows exist as draft proposals. `source_assets` is empty and `preview` is null. The gallery shows the empty frame, which is not the character.

Do not generate a character to fill the request.


## Use case: website screen

---
title: "Use case: website screen"
visibility: public
sidebar_position: 4
---

## Request

Design a website screen that respects brand rules.

## Retrieval

1. Read product public status before showing a feature.
2. Use color and type tokens by id. Do not copy a hex into the page if the token is unapproved; label the sample EXAMPLE.
3. Check contrast pairs in the token report.
4. Keep focus visible and do not use color as the only status.

## Result in this template

The documentation theme uses the EXAMPLE palette so the portal has a real theme. That theme is not a customer product UI and not an approved brand.

# BO-01 — Company & Business Plan

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** founder.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Hold the canonical description of the business: identity, customer, offer, market, model, and the assumptions behind the plan. Other modules reference these records instead of pasting a second copy.

## Decision this informs

What business this is, who it is for, and which claims are safe to repeat.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New or existing business | yes | internal | `business.identity.new_or_existing` |
| Trade name | yes | public | `business.identity.trade_name` |
| Legal name | optional | internal | `business.identity.legal_name` |
| Sector | yes | internal | `business.identity.sector` |
| Offer | yes | internal | `business.offer.summary` |
| Operating stage | yes | internal | `business.stage.current` |
| Geography | yes | internal | `business.market.geography` |
| Primary customer | yes | internal | `business.customer.primary_segment` |
| Value proposition | yes | internal | `business.offer.value_proposition` |
| Customer pains | yes | internal | `business.problem.pains` |
| Revenue model | yes | internal | `business.model.revenue` |
| Defensibility | optional | internal | `business.model.defensibility` |
| Next milestone | yes | internal | `business.plan.milestone` |
| Top risks | yes | internal | `business.plan.risks` |

## Guidance

Separate a legal name from the public trade name. If you do not know the legal name, leave it unknown.

Record the estimation method whenever a market size appears. A number without a source, date, and method stays an assumption.

Choose a profile (idea-stage, services, SaaS, marketplace, nonprofit, and so on) so later questions that do not apply can be skipped instead of forced.

Strategy lives here and in Brand Strategy as references. Execution tasks belong in the external tracker named by operations, not as a second task list in Git.

## Inputs

- Owner interview
- Existing deck or site only when the owner supplies a citation

## Artifacts

- One-page snapshot
- Business thesis
- Assumption log
- Risk notes

## Acceptance

- A reader can tell what is confirmed, estimated, and unknown.
- Brand, sales, and marketing link here instead of restating the segment.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/01-company-business-plan/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-company.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

A seed-stage education product might say its primary customer is still a hypothesis: independent adult learners, geography unknown, revenue model not chosen. That sentence is an illustration, not a default answer.

## Do

- Cite the owner and the date for every factual claim.
- Keep one primary-segment record and point brand personas at its id.
- Mark idea-stage unknowns as unknown.

## Don't

- Do not invent TAM, revenue, headcount, or founder biographies.
- Do not paste bank details, identification numbers, or customer lists.
- Do not fork a second company strategy inside the brand book.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Trade name and sector have a disposition.
- [ ] Primary customer is either described or explicitly unknown.
- [ ] Value proposition is the single canonical wording.
- [ ] Assumptions are labeled separately from verified facts.

## Dependencies

- None. This module can start from the interview.

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/business-company.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Revisit at each stage change and at least quarterly.

## Metrics

- Milestone completion
- Assumption burn-down

# BO-02 — Marketing Strategy & Planning

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** marketing.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Decide how the canonical customer and offer reach the market. This module plans; it does not restate positioning or keep a live analytics warehouse in Markdown.

## Decision this informs

Which channels, messages, and budgets are in the current plan, and which claims are allowed.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Marketing objective | yes | internal | `business.marketing.objective` |
| Channels | yes | internal | `business.marketing.channels` |
| Journey hypothesis | yes | internal | `business.marketing.journey` |
| Content pillars | optional | internal | `business.marketing.pillars` |
| Channel budget | yes | restricted | `business.marketing.budget` |
| Attribution | yes | internal | `business.marketing.attribution` |
| Availability claims | yes | internal | `business.marketing.availability_claim` |
| UTM taxonomy | optional | internal | `business.marketing.utm` |
| Primary customer | canonical reference | internal | `business.customer.primary_segment` |
| Value proposition | canonical reference | internal | `business.offer.value_proposition` |
| Geography | canonical reference | internal | `business.market.geography` |

## Guidance

Use SOSTAC as a field set: situation, objectives, strategy, tactics, action, control. It is a planning shape, not the only standard.

Channel playbooks (search, social, email, community, partners, PR, events, offline) stay empty until the channel is selected.

Separate the annual strategy from the dated plan and from execution tasks in the tracker.

Every public availability or price claim must point at the product status and the pricing record.

## Inputs

- Canonical segment
- Offer
- Geography
- Product public status

## Artifacts

- Marketing objectives
- Channel plan
- Claim rules
- Experiment backlog link

## Acceptance

- A campaign brief can be written without inventing a new audience.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/02-marketing/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-marketing.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

An EXAMPLE quarterly plan might test one organic channel and zero paid spend until a price exists. The absence of spend is a decision, not a missing number to invent.

## Do

- Reference business.customer.primary_segment and business.offer.value_proposition.
- Date every plan and mark it as a plan, not as measured performance.
- Store UTM rules as a naming convention, not as a dump of campaign URLs.

## Don't

- Do not create a second persona with a different id.
- Do not publish an unshipped feature as available.
- Do not paste ad-account credentials or customer exports.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Objectives name a metric owner and a source system.
- [ ] Channel list matches the current quarter, not a wish list presented as a commitment.
- [ ] Attribution model is either chosen or explicitly undecided.

## Dependencies

- `business-company`
- `brand-strategy`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/business-marketing.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Strategy yearly; plan monthly; results only from the analytics system.

## Metrics

- Planned channel
- Claim violations found in review

# BO-03 — Product & Service Strategy

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** product.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Describe the offer as a product or service system: jobs, scope, non-goals, readiness, and evidence. Research notes stay consented and minimal.

## Decision this informs

What is in scope, what is shipped, and what marketing must not imply.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Portfolio | yes | internal | `business.product.portfolio` |
| Jobs to be done | yes | internal | `business.product.jobs` |
| MVP boundary | yes | internal | `business.product.mvp` |
| Public status | yes | internal | `business.product.public_status` |
| Roadmap horizon | yes | internal | `business.product.roadmap` |
| Accessibility intent | yes | internal | `business.product.accessibility` |
| Activation definition | optional | internal | `business.product.activation` |
| Learning model | optional | internal | `business.product.learning_model` |
| Languages taught | optional | internal | `business.product.learning_languages` |
| Research evidence policy | yes | internal | `business.product.evidence_policy` |
| Offer | canonical reference | internal | `business.offer.summary` |
| Primary customer | canonical reference | internal | `business.customer.primary_segment` |

## Guidance

Write PRD-shaped briefs with problem, scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, and analytics events. Do not pretend a template brief is an approved PRD.

Roadmaps may use now/next/later without fake dates. Dated commitments need an owner.

Prioritization method (RICE, MoSCoW, or another) is a choice recorded here, not a hidden default.

Store interview evidence as citations and permissions, never as raw personal data.

## Inputs

- Offer summary
- Segment
- Evidence the owner chooses to cite

## Artifacts

- Portfolio note
- MVP boundary
- Public status
- Roadmap now/next/later

## Acceptance

- Design and marketing can see what is live.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/03-product-services/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-product.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: public status remains unshipped while a clickable prototype exists. The prototype is not a launch.

## Do

- Link jobs-to-be-done to the primary segment id.
- Keep public status explicit: unshipped, beta, or available.
- Record non-goals so brand creative does not advertise them.

## Don't

- Do not market a roadmap item as a live feature.
- Do not upload research recordings or respondent contact details.
- Do not invent adoption or retention numbers.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Public status is set.
- [ ] MVP boundary is written or explicitly unknown.
- [ ] Accessibility intent is stated without claiming a finished audit.

## Dependencies

- `business-company`

## Related drafts

Machine draft: `brand/generated/drafts/business-product.md`

## Completion

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Update public status at every release decision.

# BO-04 — Sales & Revenue

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** sales.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Describe how revenue is asked for and closed: motion, qualification, pricing, and handoff. Consumer paywalls and enterprise pipelines are both valid; neither is assumed.

## Decision this informs

What may be promised, discounted, and forecast.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sales motion | yes | internal | `business.sales.motion` |
| Buyer versus user | yes | internal | `business.sales.buyer` |
| Pricing summary | yes | internal | `business.sales.pricing` |
| Discount policy | optional | internal | `business.sales.discount` |
| Pipeline stages | yes | internal | `business.sales.stages` |
| Cycle assumption | optional | internal | `business.sales.cycle` |
| B2B packaging | optional | internal | `business.sales.b2b_packaging` |
| Consumer purchase path | optional | internal | `business.sales.consumer_path` |
| Revenue model | canonical reference | internal | `business.model.revenue` |
| Primary customer | canonical reference | internal | `business.customer.primary_segment` |

## Guidance

Pick a motion: self-serve, product-led, inside sales, enterprise, retail, channel, or not applicable.

Pricing is canonical here. Marketing offers reference it and must not invent a second price.

Forecasts need a date, a method, and a confidence label. A blank forecast stays blank.

B2C questions cover trial, upgrade, and subscription only when that model is chosen.

## Inputs

- Revenue model
- Offer
- Segment

## Artifacts

- Motion note
- Pricing record
- Discount rule
- Stage definitions

## Acceptance

- A seller cannot quote a number that is not in the pricing record.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/04-sales-revenue/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-sales.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: motion is undecided, so there is no quota and no script. The honest sales asset is a one-paragraph offer.

## Do

- Keep discount authority explicit.
- Point battlecards at canonical competitor notes the owner actually supplied.
- Separate pipeline stages you use from stages you might use later.

## Don't

- Do not invent conversion rates, quotas, or average deal size.
- Do not store customer lists or signed contracts with personal data.
- Do not publish a price that finance has not seen when a price exists.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Motion is chosen or not applicable.
- [ ] Pricing record is unknown, estimated, or confirmed — never implied.
- [ ] Public pages are not allowed to outrun this record.

- `business-product`

# BO-07 — Finance & Unit Economics

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** finance.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Record currency, accounting basis, and the assumptions behind any model. Figures stay unknown unless the owner supplies them with a date and a confidence label. This is not an audit.

## Decision this informs

Which financial statements are assumptions, and which systems are authoritative.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reporting currency | yes | internal | `business.finance.currency` |
| Accounting basis | yes | internal | `business.finance.basis` |
| Revenue figure | yes | restricted | `business.finance.revenue_figure` |
| Cost drivers | yes | restricted | `business.finance.costs` |
| Runway | optional | restricted | `business.finance.runway` |
| Pricing economics note | yes | internal | `business.finance.economics_note` |
| Finance system | optional | internal | `business.finance.system` |
| Scenarios | optional | internal | `business.finance.scenarios` |
| Pricing summary | canonical reference | internal | `business.sales.pricing` |
| Revenue model | canonical reference | internal | `business.model.revenue` |

## Guidance

Every number needs currency, period, source, and whether it is actual, plan, or estimate.

Do not compute a vanity LTV from missing inputs. Show the missing input instead.

Bank statements, tax identifiers, and raw ledgers do not belong in this repository.

Optimistic, base, and conservative cases are labels for scenarios the owner defines, not three invented spreadsheets.

## Inputs

- Pricing record
- Owner estimates with dates

## Artifacts

- Assumption sheet
- Scenario labels
- System-of-record pointer

## Acceptance

- A reader can see that the template contains no financial performance.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/07-finance-unit-economics/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-finance.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: reporting currency is undecided, revenue is unknown, and there is no runway claim.

## Do

- Point at the finance system of record.
- Keep restricted figures in the restricted collection.
- Say unknown.

## Don't

- Do not manufacture MRR, burn, or runway.
- Do not claim audit readiness.
- Do not store account numbers.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Currency is set or unknown.
- [ ] No restricted figure appears in a public draft.
- [ ] Pricing economics reference the sales pricing record.

# BO-10 — Growth & Experimentation

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** growth.

## Purpose

Keep a hypothesis backlog and the rules for learning. Results are recorded only after an experiment runs.

## Decision this informs

Which bets are hypotheses, and how a result becomes a decision.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.

| Marketing objective | canonical reference | internal | `business.marketing.objective` |

## Guidance

Write hypotheses with audience, change, expected signal, and guardrail.

Loops (acquisition, activation, retention, referral, revenue) reference canonical metrics.

A winning variant is not a brand rule until the owner approves the change.

## Inputs

- Marketing objective

EXAMPLE backlog item: “If the first screen states the job-to-be-done, more people finish it.” No result exists.

## Do

- Separate the backlog from the learning log.
- Name an owner for each live experiment.
- Record losers.

## Don't

- Do not invent lift, p-values, or cohort charts.
- Do not let an experiment overwrite approved copy without the approval flow.
- Do not run dark patterns as “growth”.

- [ ] Guardrails include trust and accessibility, not only conversion.

# BO-11 — Goals, KPIs, Analytics & Reviews

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** leadership.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Define objectives, metric meanings, and review cadence. Live actuals stay in the source system. This module stores definitions, targets the owner sets, and links.

## Decision this informs

What “good” means, and which number is a target rather than an actual.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |

| Plan versus actual | yes | internal | `business.goals.plan_vs_actual` |
| Next milestone | canonical reference | internal | `business.plan.milestone` |

## Guidance

A metric registry row needs id, definition, unit, formula, timezone, source, freshness, and caveats.

Targets, forecasts, and actuals are different fields. Never title an actual with a stale snapshot date hidden in prose.

Weekly and quarterly reviews can be templates until the first real review.

North-star language is optional. Do not crown a metric you cannot collect.

## Inputs

- Marketing objective
- Activation definition

- Metric registry starter
- Review cadence

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: the only objective is “learn whether the segment is real.” There is no numeric KPI.

## Do

- Name the source system for every metric you intend to use.
- Keep the planning year explicit.
- Allow a brand to have no numeric goal yet.

## Don't

- Do not paste dashboard screenshots as if they were current next year.
- Do not invent baselines.

- `business-company`

# BO-12 — Partnerships, Distribution, Risk & Investor Readiness

**Answer status in a fresh template:** not started. Guidance on this page is reusable. It is not an approved brand decision.
**Owner role:** leadership.
**Visibility of this guidance:** public. Interview answers default to internal, and some finance or partner fields are restricted.

## Purpose

Cover distribution partners, the risk register, and investor narrative only from verified claims. Confidential board material stays in a restricted collection, usually outside this repo.

## Decision this informs

Which external relationships and risks are real, and what an outsider may be told.

## How to complete this module

1. Run `npm run brand:interview`. The agent asks one eligible question at a time.
2. Read the draft it writes under `brand/generated/drafts/` or, for restricted answers, `brand/restricted/drafts/`.
3. Approve a field only after you mean it: `npm run brand:approve -- --question <id> --proof <secret>`.
4. Add real files to the asset manifest when you have them. Missing files stay missing.

## Canonical fields

| Field | Required | Sensitivity | Question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Partners | yes | internal | `business.partners.channels` |
| Revenue share | optional | restricted | `business.partners.share` |
| Risk review | yes | internal | `business.partners.risk_process` |
| External narrative | yes | internal | `business.partners.narrative` |
| Diligence index | optional | internal | `business.partners.diligence` |
| Board documents | optional | restricted | `business.partners.board_home` |
| Top risks | canonical reference | internal | `business.plan.risks` |
| Next milestone | canonical reference | internal | `business.plan.milestone` |
| Value proposition | canonical reference | internal | `business.offer.value_proposition` |

## Guidance

Partner tiers and revenue-share notes are assumptions until a signed term is cited.

Risks need a probability/impact label the owner believes, plus an owner and a review date. Unknown probability stays unknown.

Pitch outlines pull from approved or clearly estimated fields. They do not create new traction numbers.

Diligence indexes link to sources. They do not embed the data room.

## Inputs

- Offer
- Milestone
- Risks
- Finance unknowns

## Artifacts

- Partner note
- Risk register
- Pitch outline rules
- Diligence index

## Acceptance

- A pitch cannot show a number that finance marked unknown.

## Fill-in record

The empty record is `brand/business-os/12-partnerships-risk-investors/record.yaml`. Live answers are stored in `brand/instance/` and the generated draft `brand/generated/drafts/business-partnerships.md`, so editing this overview does not approve a fact.

## Worked example

> EXAMPLE — illustrative only. Not this brand’s position, offer, price, legal status, or artwork.

EXAMPLE: there are no partners, no round, and no data room. The narrative is “pre-evidence”.

## Do

- Keep investor documents restricted.
- Reuse the canonical milestone and offer.
- Name distribution channels you actually have.

## Don't

- Do not invent traction, logos of customers, or a round size.
- Do not commit board decks with personal data.
- Do not treat a partner conversation as a signed channel.

## Review checklist

- [ ] Narrative uses only sourced claims.
- [ ] Risks link to the company risk note.
- [ ] Restricted board location is a system name, not the files.

## Dependencies

- `business-company`
- `business-finance`
- `business-legal`

## Related drafts

Coverage counts required fields that have any honest disposition, including unknown. Approval counts only fields a permitted person has approved. `npm run brand:status` prints both. Unanswered is not approved.

## Update cadence

Review before any external fundraising conversation.

## Metrics

- Open risks
- Unsourced pitch claims
